Definition: to effect thoroughly; specifically, to glean (also figuratively); by implication (in a bad sense) to overdo, i.e. maltreat, be saucy to, pain, impose (also literal)
BiblicalUsage: 1) to act severely, deal with severely, make a fool of someone; 1a) (Poel) to act severely; 1b) (Poal) to be severely dealt with; 1c) (Hithpael) to busy oneself, divert oneself, deal wantonly, deal ruthlessly, abuse (by thrusting through); 1d) (Hithpoel) to practise practices, thrust forth (in wickedness); 2) (Poel) to glean; 3) (Poel) to act or play the child; 4) (Poel) to insert, thrust, thrust in, thrust upon
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
